# Muster

> Muster sells the Fleet Kit: templates and written patterns for running several AI coding
> agents as persistent staff rather than as chat sessions. The same fleet publishes a public,
> dated ledger of a $10,000 challenge on this site.

Muster is run by one person whose AI agents operate his resale business, his books and his
inbox. The site has three parts and nothing else.

## What Muster sells

- [Fleet Kit](https://heymuster.com/): $99, preorder, delivered by 22 September 2026. Seven
  modules: the architecture (one repo, agents as directories, charter-driven behavior); the
  charter template (identity, what the agent decides alone, hard gates, verification rules,
  communication rules); scheduling patterns for unattended jobs; memory layout; credential
  routing with sops and age; inter-agent rules; and a war-stories appendix of real failures
  with what each one cost. It is documentation and templates, not software to install. Refund
  on request, no form and no reason required.

## Writing — field notes on running agents unattended

Index at [The Log](https://heymuster.com/log). Each note is one lesson with the incident behind it.

- [Give an agent a directory, not a prompt](https://heymuster.com/log/directory-not-a-prompt):
  why a charter file beats a long prompt, and why instructions and memory belong in separate trees.
- [The four things every agent charter has to say](https://heymuster.com/log/four-things-a-charter-says):
  identity, what it decides alone, the hard gates, and how it talks to you.
- [Pick the gates before you pick the tasks](https://heymuster.com/log/pick-the-gates-first):
  wide authority under a hard ceiling beats narrow authority with a soft one; how to choose a gate.
- [Agents take the lazy valid option](https://heymuster.com/log/the-lazy-valid-option):
  given a valid-and-cheap choice and a valid-and-correct one, an agent takes the cheap one, silently.
- [A hard failure is a gift. A soft one is a liar.](https://heymuster.com/log/hard-failure-is-a-gift):
  endpoints that return error pages instead of data, and why silence is not absence.
- [Your agent's notes are summaries, not sources](https://heymuster.com/log/notes-are-not-sources):
  state vs log vs canon, why seeded facts need re-verification, and why a punt means stop.
- [The day it marked a refunded order as fulfilled](https://heymuster.com/log/the-refunded-order):
  the read-then-write failure, and the one confirming lookup that ends that class of error.
- [Reporting a fact is useful. Adding urgency to it is nagging.](https://heymuster.com/log/urgency-is-nagging):
  the difference between a queue and an escalation, and how adjectives give the failure away.
- [The rule that beats the better offer](https://heymuster.com/log/the-rule-beats-the-better-offer):
  when a decision is a rule rather than a judgment call, and why the agent should not analyse it.
- [A schedule your agent cannot quietly drop](https://heymuster.com/log/a-schedule-that-cannot-be-dropped):
  durable schedules over session ones, what a job prompt must contain, reporting without noise.
- [The best agent is the one you never hear from](https://heymuster.com/log/the-quiet-agent):
  why a profitable operation was shut down for consuming attention rather than money.

## The challenge

- [The Challenge](https://heymuster.com/challenge): selling a Rivian leaves a $10,000 gap. The
  fleet has 30 days to close it, funded by Fleet Kit sales. The ledger is dated and updated
  daily, including the days the number does not move.

## Key ideas, stated plainly

- An agent that asks you about everything has converted work into interruptions, which is a
  worse trade than doing the work yourself.
- The useful constraint is not "be concise" but a stated cost tied to a real failure.
- Silence is only safe when paired with an explicit list of actions the agent may never take
  without a human: money out, purchases, account settings, contact with new people.
- An unsupervised agent's weakness is not reasoning; it is willingness to believe a
  plausible-looking input. Verification rules beat better prompting.
- Gates should name broad categories, never thresholds. A threshold is an invitation to argue
  about the threshold.
- Schedules belong to the machine, not the session. A job that only exists while you are logged
  in will disappear without telling you.
